## At a glance
| harness | what it does | checks beyond "does not crash" | statements |
|---|---|---|---|
| [fuzz_codec](fuzz_codec/) | Despite the header comment ('Round-trips the AMQP codecs'), nothing is compared: first byte %3 selects method/properties/table; the payload is decoded, and on AMQP_STATUS_OK re-encoded into a 1 MiB scratch buffer (amqp_encode_method/properties/table) and, for tables, cloned with amqp_table_clone. The encoder return codes and outputs are discarded and never compared with the input bytes or the decoded struct. | none | 15 |
| [fuzz_handle_input](fuzz_handle_input/) | Feeds the input to amqp_handle_input() frame by frame (up to 4096 iterations), advancing by the consumed count; stops on res <= 0. No result checked beyond the loop control. | none | 15 |
| [fuzz_method_decode](fuzz_method_decode/) | First 4 bytes are the method id; amqp_decode_method() on the rest into a pool; the status is stored in unused_result and ignored. | none | 15 |
| [fuzz_properties_decode](fuzz_properties_decode/) | First 2 bytes are the class id; amqp_decode_properties() on the rest; status ignored. | none | 15 |
| [fuzz_server](fuzz_server/) | In-memory socket class serves the input as broker bytes; amqp_login() runs the full client handshake (Start/Tune/Open). The returned amqp_rpc_reply_t is ignored. | none | 15 |
| [fuzz_table](fuzz_table/) | amqp_decode_table() on the whole input; result ignored. | none | 15 |
| [fuzz_url](fuzz_url/) | NUL-terminates a copy of the input and calls amqp_parse_url(); the return code and the parsed amqp_connection_info are ignored. | none | 13 |

Not included: **api-driver** (held from this release); **fuzz_read_message** (not built yet).

## What the statements say, for rabbitmq-c
- **`<build>_halts`**: on every input on which the build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise: an input that needs more is not covered), and when the environment refuses nothing it is not forced to, every execution exits with status 0 or 2, without crashing, failing an assertion, hanging or tripping its sanitizer.
- **`<build>_halts_may_fail`**: with no memory premise, and even if any request is refused at any point, every execution exits, with any status. Stated for the plain and UBSan builds only.
- **`<build>_agrees`**: on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding its budget (a premise), neither build reaches an error, and the two have the same set of observable behaviours: every sequence of writes and exit status one can show, the other can too. A sanitizer report aborts, so this rules out every error the sanitizer build's configuration detects. It does not rule out a run that never ends; only a halts statement does.
- **`<build>_disagrees_at_most b`**: for inputs drawn from the harness's `Distribution.v`, the plain and sanitizer builds disagree with probability at most *b*.
- **`<build>_agreement_decidable`**: some riscv64 program decides exactly the finite inputs on which the two builds agree. A program that does so, with a bound on how often it rejects, is a route to a disagreement bound (docs/statements.md).

## Get and run the binaries
    ./oft fetch rabbitmq-c
    ./oft verify-sha rabbitmq-c

By hand: download `rabbitmq-c-bin.tar.zst` from release [v2026.10.0](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.10.0), unpack it into `projects/rabbitmq-c/bin/`, and check each file against its SHA-256 in the harness's `harness.yaml`. Each binary is run as `<file> <input-file>` under qemu-user 10; an OSS-Fuzz testcase needs the six-byte header `00 00 00 00 00 00` in front ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)).

## How these binaries were built
- Library: [alanxz/rabbitmq-c](https://github.com/alanxz/rabbitmq-c) at `6ddbdb2d8c1f63dcd3eb65c7a33d36b1d6417eed`, built with CMake
- Harnesses: unmodified
- Everywhere: static riscv64 compiled for RV64G, musl, clang 20.1.8 with `-Os -g`, and a small driver that reads the input file ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)). The sanitizer flags and options are in [docs/building.md](../../docs/building.md). Each harness page lists what else its builds change, and which of its checks were confirmed in the binaries.
- Builder image: `ghcr.io/theorem-labs/oss-fuzz-theorems-toolchain@sha256:6a6b4816865c7ec61801ae0fcab6d9c81a599ffcb20616576a9c668abd8b0a7b`. A binary whose SHA-256 differs after a rebuild with it is a bug: please open an issue.
